verified: Real private upload and MP3 processing → rights declaration → exact-media review → explicit publication → public catalog/range playback/offline download → staff revocation, on both databases.

Versioned rights attestation timestamp retained in durable submit audit; declaration is not independent verification. Every submission/approval/publication rehashes actual stored derivative bytes without full buffering.
Server-derived creator/staff roles and ownership, no self-review/public privilege provisioning, narrowly scoped review output streaming, controlled reasons/notes, admin-only creator suspension.
Revision/UUID-receipt state transitions, duplicate mutation replay returns current state without new audit, conflicting review and publish/revoke races, synthetic audit failure transaction rollback.

Content/chapter revisions and exact source/head/output snapshots fence changed/removed/corrupt media; creator suspension and reactivation never restore revoked visibility; repeated old publish receipt and stale production processing handler cannot republish.

Real Redis cache population/hits, publication revision invalidation, intentionally forced old Redis revision plus live SQL filtering after revocation. Public MP3 server gate does not trust catalog caches.
Public MP3 full/range/invalid-range/HEAD, actual decoded durations/byte metadata, source WAV preserved, private-owner endpoints deny staff bypass; public objects omit owner/private keys.
Published creator favorites, playlists and analytics work; revoke hides inaccessible membership without deleting records/events. Existing progress/idempotency/queue/PWA/restart suites pass.

Both additive publication migrations preserve already processed private media without granting visibility. Actual SQLite→PostgreSQL import preserves audit but withdraws publication and invalidates unavailable private bytes. Populated 32-table PostgreSQL backup restores exact fingerprints, including publication/audit/receipts; old manifests remain supported.

Final clean-install full application/safety suite, production build, formatting and 170 browser groups passed. Real worker SIGKILL/restart, outbox/Redis-loss recovery and stale-fence checks remain in the full application suite; the publication-specific stale delivery check invokes the production handler after revocation.

contract.reviewUnit: Story-level, all active chapters and exact immutable derivatives
contract.lifecycle: draft → submitted → approved → published → unpublished; rejected/withdrawn/revoked supported
contract.mutationPreconditions: expectedRevision (initial 0) + UUID requestId; existing session/CSRF/account scope
contract.republish: Unchanged voluntary unpublish may reuse approval; changes or staff revocation/suspension require fresh submission/reapproval
contract.privacy: Revocation blocks new server-authorized public reads/downloads and preserves listening records. Previously downloaded/buffered/exported/disconnected copies cannot reliably be recalled.

limitations: Local private filesystem only; no new public deployment, remote Actions run, production-capacity or cross-browser evidence.
Submission/approval/publication perform bounded streaming integrity I/O inside owner-locked transactions; 100-chapter high-contention latency is not benchmarked and requires M3/M4 hardening.

Previously downloaded/buffered/in-flight copies cannot be recalled. Offline or HEAD-timeout playback can retain a prior device copy; successful online 404/410 blocks playback and removes cached audio. Cached metadata/exported files may remain.
Checksummed readiness is not rights verification or automated content moderation. No payments, scheduled release, AI, public object store/CDN or automated takedown notices.

Audit has no HTTP update/delete API, but database operators can modify rows; no cryptographic tamper-proof claim. UI lists 50 pending submissions and last 100 audit entries; long-term retention/export remain follow-up.

SQL and filesystem are not jointly atomic. Backup requires matching private-volume snapshot; restored older backups must reconcile later revocations before public access. Subsequent disk corruption/outages need recovery/monitoring.

New publishing workflow was not separately container-deployed or load-tested. Existing real worker recovery tests ran; optional resource-intensive Docker/system/load/SMTP checks were not rerun for this milestone.
